The test image shows a tomato compound leaf with:
- Widespread interveinal chlorosis (pale green/yellow leaves, veins slightly greener)
- Brown necrotic areas, especially at leaf margins and tips
- One severely affected leaflet (left) with large brown necrotic/curled tissue
- Scattered small brown spots on leaflets

This pattern of interveinal yellowing + marginal necrosis strongly suggests a vascular/systemic disease. Top candidates: **Verticillium_Wilt**, Late Blight, or Leaf Mold. I'll use my 1 reference view on Verticillium Wilt.

The Verticillium Wilt reference matches well: asymmetric interveinal chlorosis, marginal/tip browning progressing inward, with small dark spots scattered on the leaf surface. The test image shows the same pattern across multiple leaflets at different infection stages — some just yellowing, one severely necrotized.

Reference image confirms the asymmetric yellowing and marginal browning pattern. No concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight), no white mold (ruling out Gray Mold/Late Blight undersides), and no distinct olive mold patches (ruling out Leaf Mold)."}
